title: Use the Australia Take Home Pay Calculator to Compare the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay with the Australia take home pay calculator. Compare the National Minimum Wage and award rates, including casual load
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, yielding $1,004.90 per week and $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I use the Australia take home pay calculator on this site?
faqs.a: On the timesheet page, enter your base hourly rate in the box. If you are a casual employee, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of that base rate. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly and annual gross pay based on a 38-hour week. It also estimates tax, Medicare levy and superannuation, giving you an approximate take-home amount. Remember, the calculator assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates or salary sacrifice.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the minimum hourly rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult employee. Award rates are industry- or occupation-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a retail award might have a higher base rate. The Australia take home pay calculator can help you compare both by entering the relevant hourly rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated in the take-home pay estimate?
faqs.a: Superannuation is calculated at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. The calculator applies the 12% rate up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross pay is $60,000, the estimated super contribution is $7,200. This amount is not included in your take-home pay because it goes into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understand Your Pay with the Australia Take Home Pay Calculator

Whether you are an employee negotiating a salary or a contractor comparing offers, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly and weekly pay is essential. The [Australia take home pay calculator](/topics/take-home) on this site makes it simple. You enter your base hourly rate, choose whether you are casual (which adds 25% loading), and the calculator does the rest. It uses the standard full-time hours of 38 per week, multiplies by 52 weeks, and then estimates tax, Medicare and superannuation.

### The Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The core calculation is straightforward: annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, that means multiplying your hourly rate by 1,976 (38 × 52). For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates or allowances.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making their minimum rate $33.05 per hour.

However, many employees are covered by an award – a specific industry or occupation minimum determined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Award rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For instance, a hospitality award might have a base rate of $28 per hour for a full-time adult, while a building and construction award could be $32 per hour. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides more details on current rates.

When you use the Australia take home pay calculator, you can enter any award rate to see your estimated pay. The calculator does not invent a job median – it uses the hourly rate you provide. If you are unsure of your award rate, check your award or enterprise agreement, or consult the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should include a 25% loading to compensate for the lack of paid leave. The calculator has a checkbox to add this loading on top of the base rate you enter. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – always enter the base rate and tick the box.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. The calculator estimates this amount separately. It is not deducted from your take-home pay; it is an additional contribution your employer makes to your super fund.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

The calculator uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil tax on the first $18,200, then 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The calculator applies the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employees are paid fortnightly. The calculator shows your fortnightly gross pay as weekly pay multiplied by two. For example, at the National Minimum Wage, weekly gross is $1,004.90, so fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, your take-home pay will be lower. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page gives more detail on deductions.

### Example: Comparing Minimum Wage and an Award Rate

Suppose you are a full-time adult employee working 38 hours per week. At the National Minimum Wage ($26.44/hr), your annual gross is $52,254.80. Estimated tax and Medicare on that income would be about $5,508, leaving a take-home of roughly $46,747 per year. Your fortnightly take-home would be about $1,798.

Now consider an award rate of $30 per hour. Annual gross becomes $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. Tax and Medicare on $59,280 are approximately $7,128, giving a take-home of $52,152 per year, or $2,006 per fortnight. The difference of $208 per fortnight highlights the value of knowing your correct award rate.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [timesheet](/) page is the home of the Australia take home pay calculator. You can adjust the hours per week if you work part-time (the default is 38 hours). The calculator also shows the super contribution estimate. Remember, the results are an estimate only – your actual pay may vary due to overtime, allowances, salary sacrifice or other factors.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Further Reading

For more detailed pay guides and award rates, visit the [pay guides](/blog) page. You can also explore the [reference tables](/data) for more data on average earnings from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides the ABS Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026: full-time adult ordinary time $2,083.7 per week. All employees total earnings $1,579.2 per week (includes part-time). These figures are averages, not a job median.

Use the Australia take home pay calculator to make informed decisions about your pay. Compare the National Minimum Wage with your award rate, understand the impact of casual loading, and see how super adds to your total remuneration.
